content.overview: The final lesson combines safety, biosecurity, controlled instructions, traceability, equipment care, records and handoff into one realistic Technician I workflow.

vocabulary.definition: The collection of current instructions, assignments, records, identifiers and supporting information used to complete a task or shift.
Prioritization of conditions so urgent safety, biosecurity, identity or process risks are addressed first.
Demonstrating multiple competencies together in a realistic workflow rather than as isolated facts.

sections.title: Read the whole situation before acting
sections.body: The case contains competing priorities: a planned movement, a safety concern, a sanitation entry requirement, a hold, an inventory mismatch, an equipment alarm and incomplete prior-shift documentation. Learners identify which conditions block downstream work before beginning the first task on the list.

sections.title: Sequence, document and hand off
sections.body: The learner follows supplied SOPs, completes routine actions within authority, preserves identity, records what actually occurs and escalates unresolved conditions. The case is complete only when the resulting records show what was done, what could not be done, why, who was notified and what the next shift must address.

workedExamples: A plant move is delayed because the destination is held and one identifier mismatches; both controls are resolved through the proper authorities before movement.
An equipment alarm receives only the permitted external check and a maintenance-ready escalation, not an unauthorized repair.
commonMistakes: Starting the first assigned task before checking restrictions and identity.
Treating documentation as optional because the physical work was completed.
content.practicalApplication: Complete the integrated course case by prioritizing a work packet, identifying hazards and restrictions, preparing PPE and sanitation, resolving or escalating identity issues, performing an operator-level equipment check, documenting a deviation and writing the final handoff.
content.summary: Course 1 culminates in integrated performance: work safely, protect biosecurity and identity, follow controlled instructions, stay within authority, create trustworthy records and communicate unresolved conditions clearly.

blocks.title: Capstone rule: do not start with the first line on the task list
blocks.body: Read the whole work packet before acting. A hold, restricted-entry condition, identity mismatch, sanitation failure, or unsafe equipment condition can block a downstream task even when that task appears first on the schedule.

steps.title: Review the packet and prior handoff
steps.body: Identify assigned work, current instructions, open items, alarms, holds, restrictions, and time-sensitive events.

steps.title: Check safety and entry controls
steps.body: Confirm hazards, PPE, chemical information, restricted-entry status, and conditions that require stop-work or escalation.

steps.title: Verify the current controlled instruction
steps.body: Confirm the applicable SOP or work order and reconcile any conflict before proceeding.

steps.title: Verify identity and destination
steps.body: Match physical identifiers, source, destination, count or quantity, and current status before movement or processing.

steps.title: Prepare sanitation and biosecurity controls
steps.body: Complete the required entry, tool, surface, and workflow controls before introducing people or materials.

steps.title: Perform only authorized routine work
steps.body: Stay within the assigned operator and Technician I boundary; servicing, hazardous access, release decisions, and other higher-authority actions are escalated.

steps.title: Capture facts as they occur
steps.body: Record measurements, movements, observations, exceptions, and corrections with enough context to remain reconstructable.

steps.title: Stop or escalate when acceptance criteria fail
steps.body: Do not manufacture completion, clear holds without authority, or alter records to make physical reality appear compliant.

steps.title: Reconcile physical and recorded status
steps.body: Confirm that identifiers, quantities, locations, and open deviations agree with the actual state before closing the work.

steps.title: Hand off every unresolved condition
steps.body: Transfer exact identity, factual status, notifications, next actions, and timing using the site's controlled handoff process.

blocks.title: Work-packet triage
rows: Planned movement is blocked until authorized release
Do not move material; verify hold and escalate to the responsible role
One source tag does not match the movement order
Identity could be lost or assigned incorrectly
Stop the affected movement and preserve both physical and recorded state
Sanitation station lacks the approved product
Required biosecurity preparation may not be achievable
Do not substitute an unapproved product; follow the site contingency or escalate
Crop process may be affected; fault cause is not yet established
Capture alarm context, perform permitted checks only, and use the maintenance path
The historical observation cannot be recreated as contemporaneous data
Preserve the missing status and follow the late-entry or missing-data procedure
Add useful current observations; do not bypass the ticket with unauthorized servicing

blocks.title: Which issue blocks the planned plant move?
blocks.setting: At shift start you receive a plant-movement order. The destination room is on hold, one source tag does not match the order, the sanitation station is missing the approved product, and a pump alarm is active elsewhere.
blocks.prompt: What should happen before the move begins?
options: Start moving the correctly tagged plants and resolve the rest later
Clear the destination hold yourself because the movement is scheduled
Resolve or escalate the hold, identity mismatch, and sanitation readiness before beginning the movement; handle the pump only within the separate permitted operator process
Ignore the sanitation issue because it is unrelated to identity
blocks.answer: Resolve or escalate the hold, identity mismatch, and sanitation readiness before beginning the movement; handle the pump only within the separate permitted operator process.
blocks.feedback: Several controls independently block or condition the movement. The task order does not override hold status, identity control, biosecurity requirements, or equipment authorization boundaries.

blocks.title: Integrated performance versus task completion only

left.label: Integrated performance
left.body: Checks restrictions first, follows current instructions, protects identity, works within authority, records facts as they occur, reconciles status, and hands off unresolved conditions.

right.label: Task completion only
right.body: Focuses on finishing the visible physical task even when controls conflict, documentation is incomplete, identity is uncertain, or the next action exceeds authorization.

blocks.title: Capstone evidence packet
blocks.description: The learner should leave a reconstructable trail showing both completed work and intentionally unresolved work.

fields.label: Priority list
fields.value: Ranked safety, biosecurity, identity, equipment, and production concerns

fields.label: Controlled-instruction check
fields.value: Current SOP/work-order verification and any conflict identified

fields.label: Material movement decision
fields.value: Proceed, hold, or escalate with identity and destination evidence

fields.label: Equipment note
fields.value: Asset, alarm/fault context, permitted checks, safe action, and maintenance escalation

fields.label: Deviation / incomplete-work record
fields.value: What occurred, what did not occur, and why the status remains open

fields.label: Final reconciliation
fields.value: Physical identity, location, count/quantity, and recorded status comparison

fields.label: Shift handoff
fields.value: Exact open items, notifications, next actions, timing, and ownership where known

blocks.note: A capstone answer is not stronger because everything is marked complete. It is stronger when the final records accurately show what was completed and what still requires authorized action.

blocks.title: Complete the integrated Technician I case
blocks.instructions: Use the supplied work packet as if you were starting a real shift. Produce the evidence a supervisor or incoming technician would need to understand every decision without relying on your memory.
prompts: Identify every condition that blocks another task and explain the dependency.
Classify each response as routine action, stop/hold, escalation, maintenance referral, or higher-authority decision.
Show how identity is preserved through the movement decision.
Write the maintenance-ready equipment escalation without declaring an unsupported root cause.
Document the missed measurement without inventing data.
Reconcile the final physical and recorded state.
Write a two-way-ready final handoff that makes unresolved work visible.
blocks.artifact: Completed integrated work packet with priority map, decision record, reconciliation, deviation documentation, equipment escalation, and final handoff

blocks.title: Course 1 standard
blocks.body: Technician I competence is not knowing every answer or independently clearing every problem. It is executing routine work safely and consistently, protecting identity and records, recognizing abnormal conditions, and escalating correctly instead of improvising beyond role authority.
